chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abu Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him), 'How is the greeting to be upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at his grave?'
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Say, 'The greeting be upon the Messenger of Allah.'
The greeting be upon you, O Beloved of Allah! The greeting be upon you, O elite of Allah! The greeting be upon you, O trustworthy one of Allah!'
I testify that you preached to your community, and struggled in the Way of Allah, and worshipped Him until conviction came to you.
So, may Allah recompense you with the most superior of what He would recompense a Prophet for his community.
O Allah! Send Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, superior than what You blessed upon Ibrahim and the progeny of Ibrahim, You being the Praised One, the Glorious.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct supplication to recite when visiting the grave of the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi outlines the comprehensive ritual greeting (Tahiyyah) for the Prophet at his grave, emphasizing titles that highlight his divine selection as 'Chosen One' and 'Trustee of God.' It integrates personal testimony of his lifelong struggle and worship with a petition for divine recompense, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of prophetic status after death. The supplication concludes by linking the Prophet's blessings to those of Ibrahim, underscoring the familial and spiritual lineage central to Shia theology.
